title: FBISE Annual Exam Simulator 04 (Heroes & Applied Grammar)
subject: english-12

questions.question: According to Dean Hawkes, why is a boy forced into medicine or engineering by his parents likely to fail?

options.A: His natural aptitudes and genuine interest lie elsewhere, causing chronic lack of motivation.
options.B: Medical and engineering programs refuse students selected by parents.
options.C: His parents refuse to provide tuition fees.
options.D: College faculty actively discourage parental guidance.

questions.explanation: A boy whose heart is in theatrical production or writing will have no enthusiasm for anatomy or calculus, leading to academic paralysis.

questions.question: What is the definition of a 'critical attitude' developed through scientific education?

options.A: Finding fault in every person's behavior
options.B: Evaluating claims based on verified evidence rather than hearsay, tradition, or emotional bias
options.C: Criticizing literary masterpieces in academic journals
options.D: Refusing to believe in scientific laws

questions.explanation: A critical, open-minded attitude means suspending judgement until reproducible evidence is available to confirm or deny an assertion.

questions.question: When Jerome went to the British Museum reading room to study a specific ailment, what disease was he researching initially?

options.A: Hay fever
options.B: Typhoid
options.C: Cholera

questions.explanation: He looked up Hay Fever, but started browsing the medical book alphabetically from 'A' to 'Z', diagnosing himself with every single malady.

questions.question: What was the psychological impact of Daiches receiving an unexpected half-holiday during school?

options.A: It was greeted with ecstatic delight because unearned, spontaneous freedom felt richer than scheduled vacations.
options.B: It caused anxiety because homework could not be handed in.
options.C: He spent it studying in the library.

questions.explanation: An unexpected half-holiday granted for a special occasion felt miraculously sweet and liberating to young students.

questions.question: What is the primary engine of the modern global 'population explosion' according to McKenzie?

options.A: A sudden, massive increase in the biological birth rate
options.B: A steep and dramatic drop in the death rate—especially infant mortality—brought about by modern medicine, antibiotics, and public sanitation
options.C: Global immigration to Mars
options.D: Government subsidies for large families in western Europe

questions.explanation: The population boom is not caused by women having more babies, but by medical science keeping infants alive and extending human longevity.

questions.question: What is the grammatical term for the underlined construction: 'Entering the bank, my hands began to tremble'?

options.A: Correct absolute clause
options.B: Dangling participle (illogical modifier, as hands cannot enter a bank)
options.C: Gerundial noun phrase

questions.explanation: The subject of the main clause ('hands') is not the agent of 'entering', making it a classic dangling modifier error.

questions.question: How did Christopher survive a fierce sandstorm (simoom) in the open desert?

options.A: By running toward the oasis
options.B: By lying flat under a heavy blanket behind the vehicle's tires, breathing through cloth to avoid suffocating on flying sand
options.C: By climbing a telephone pole

questions.explanation: During a simoom, blinding sand tears skin and suffocates lungs; travelers must lie prone and cover their faces until the gale subsides.

questions.question: What is the synonym of 'arduous' as applied to Christopher's desert journey?

options.A: Effortless and breezy
options.B: Demanding, exhausting, and filled with great exertion
options.C: Short and trivial

questions.explanation: 'Arduous' means requiring strenuous effort, difficult, and physically taxing.

questions.question: What personal physical handicap did Louis Pasteur overcome during the peak of his scientific career?

options.A: He suffered a severe stroke at age 46 that left his left side permanently paralyzed, yet he continued laboratory work for decades.
options.B: He was completely blind from birth.
options.C: He lost both legs in the Franco-Prussian war.

questions.explanation: Despite being semi-paralyzed from a cerebral hemorrhage in 1868, Pasteur's iron will drove him to make his greatest discoveries in anthrax and rabies.

questions.question: What was Pasteur's answer to critics who claimed spontaneous generation occurred in boiled broth?

options.A: He showed that if air entering the flask was filtered or passed through a bent swan-neck curve, dust carrying microbes could not enter, and the broth remained sterile indefinitely.
options.B: He added poison to the broth.
options.C: He sealed the flasks inside iron boxes.
options.D: He performed his experiments at midnight.

questions.explanation: The swan-neck flask experiment proved that gravity trapped dust particles in the bend, keeping the broth perfectly clear and free of microbial life.

questions.question: In what year did Mustafa Kemal Atatürk pass away, leaving behind a modern, sovereign secular republic?

options.A: 10 November 1938 at Dolmabahçe Palace, Istanbul
options.B: 1 January 1923
options.C: 14 August 1947

questions.explanation: Atatürk died on 10 November 1938, mourned globally as one of the greatest state-builders and military geniuses of the twentieth century.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the word 'capitulations' that were abolished at Lausanne?

options.A: Military surrenders by soldiers in the trenches
options.B: Humiliating legal and financial privileges granted to foreign nationals in the Ottoman Empire, exempting them from local courts and taxes
options.C: Architectural drawings of the palace
options.D: The capital letters of the alphabet

questions.explanation: Capitulations were unequal treaties exempting European merchants from Turkish laws, which Kemal insisted on abolishing completely.

questions.question: Who was Mrs. Wickett in relation to Brookfield School?

options.A: A former linen-room maid at the school in whose cozy cottage across the road Chips rented rooms after retirement
options.B: The wife of the school governor
options.C: The town's mayor

questions.explanation: Mrs. Wickett had worked in the school linen-room and provided Chips with affectionate care and boarding in his sunset years.

questions.question: In Hilton's narrative, how is time measured in Mr. Chips' retirement?

options.A: By the Greenwich meridian radio broadcast
options.B: By the bells of Brookfield School, signaling chapel, call-over, lunch, and prep across the street
options.C: By a grandfather clock that ran backwards
options.D: By the daily arrival of the milkman

questions.explanation: Chips lived his post-retirement life entirely attuned to Brookfield's daily schedule, marking off the hours as the chapel chimes rang out.

questions.question: What is the Latin pronunciation debate that symbolized the clash between Chips and Ralston?

options.A: Old traditional English pronunciation ('vicissim' as 'vy-sis-sim') versus the new reformed continental pronunciation ('wee-kees-seem')
options.B: Whether to translate Latin into French or German
options.C: Whether Latin should be sung or whispered

questions.explanation: Ralston championed the newly introduced classical Italian/continental pronunciation, whereas Chips considered it an unnecessary fad that made boys say 'Kikero' instead of 'Cicero'.

questions.question: In Hilton's narrative, what is meant by 'the Governors'?

options.A: The British Cabinet ministers
options.B: The governing board of trustees who held ultimate legal and financial control over the school
options.C: The municipal police chiefs

questions.explanation: The Board of Governors were the trustees and benefactors who appointed headmasters and set institutional policy.

questions.question: What did the doctor mean when he said Chips died of 'old age'?

options.A: He suffered from no disease or pain; his vital clock simply wound down peacefully like a natural sunset.
options.B: He had contracted influenza.
options.C: He died of starvation.

questions.explanation: Chips suffered from no organic illness; his gentle, tired heart simply ceased beating after a full, completed life.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence:

options.A: Hardly had Chips entered the hall when the boys rose to their feet.
options.B: Hardly had Chips entered the hall than the boys rose to their feet.
options.C: Hardly Chips had entered the hall when the boys rose to their feet.
options.D: Hardly did Chips entered the hall when the boys rose.

questions.explanation: Negative adverbial inversion: 'Hardly had + subject + V3 ... when' is the correct correlative construction.

questions.question: Identify the correct sentence regarding collective nouns:

options.A: The jury has reached its verdict unanimously.
options.B: The jury have reached its verdict unanimously.
options.C: The jury has reached their verdict unanimously.
options.D: The juries has reached its verdict.

questions.explanation: When a collective noun acts as a unified body, it takes a singular verb ('has') and a singular pronoun ('its').

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence:

options.A: The sceneries of Murree are breathtaking.
options.B: The scenery of Murree is breathtaking.
options.C: The sceneries of Murree is breathtaking.
options.D: A scenery of Murree are breathtaking.

questions.explanation: 'Scenery' is an uncountable noun with no plural form; it takes a singular verb ('is').
